_description: Permanent magnet generator, rectifier, DC bus power balance, and inverter equations for the series hybrid electrical system.

equations.name: Generator Electrical Power Output
equations.description: Electrical power output of generator from mechanical shaft input. The generator converts gearbox shaft power to AC electrical power.

reference.text: Gieras, J.F. — Permanent Magnet Motor Technology. CRC Press. §10.3

equations.name: Generator Internal EMF (3-phase PM generator)
equations.description: EMF generated by PM generator. Determines AC output voltage before rectification. Phase voltage must be matched to DC bus through rectifier diode drops.

phi.name: Power factor angle
phi.notes: cos(phi) = power factor. For PM: cos(phi) ≈ 0.95

equations.name: Rectifier DC Output Voltage
equations.description: DC bus voltage after 3-phase full-wave rectification. Converts AC generator output to DC for the motor inverter and battery charging.

V_diode.name: Diode forward voltage drop
V_diode.notes: Per diode. Two diodes in series per phase leg.

equations.active_vs_passive: GARUN uses active rectifier (4-quadrant) for bidirectional power flow (charging battery from generator, or feeding generator as motor for windmill check).

reference.text: Mohan, N. — Power Electronics: Converters, Applications, and Design §3.3. Wiley.

equations.name: DC Bus Power Balance
equations.description: Kirchhoff's current law equivalent for power at the DC bus. At every time step, generated power + battery discharge = motor demand + battery charging + DC losses. The energy management system (EMS) decides the split.

P_loss_DC.name: DC bus losses
P_loss_DC.notes: Cable resistance, bus capacitor losses. Typically < 1%.

EMS_control_modes.hybrid_boost: P_gen_DC + P_batt_dis = P_motor_DC. Both sources active.
EMS_control_modes.charge_sustaining: P_gen_DC = P_motor_DC + P_batt_chg. Generator also charges battery.
EMS_control_modes.peak_shaving: P_gen_DC = P_threshold. P_batt_dis = P_motor_DC - P_threshold (if P_motor > P_threshold).

reference.text: Ehsani, Gao, Emadi — Modern Electric, Hybrid Electric, and Fuel Cell Vehicles. CRC Press. §6.3

equations.name: Rectifier Efficiency
equations.description: Rectifier power conversion efficiency. For active IGBT rectifier, switching losses dominate. Higher switching frequency → lower harmonic distortion but higher losses.

reference.text: Rashid, M.H. — Power Electronics Handbook. Elsevier. §17.2

equations.name: Inverter Output Power (to motor)
equations.description: Power delivered to motor from inverter. Inverter converts DC bus voltage to 3-phase AC at variable frequency and amplitude to control motor speed and torque.

switching_frequency.trade_off: Higher f → lower motor current ripple + smaller filter → but higher switching losses → lower eta_inv

equations.name: Total Electrical Path Efficiency (generator to shaft)
equations.description: End-to-end efficiency from engine gearbox shaft to motor shaft, through the full electrical path. Used to compute fuel equivalent cost of electrical power.

GARUN_result.interpretation: For every 100 kW of shaft power from engine going through the electrical path, 83.2 kW reaches the motor shaft. 16.8 kW is heat in generator + rectifier + inverter + motor windings.

comparison_to_direct_drive.but: Series hybrid gains: TET management, all-electric loiter, weight redistribution, peak shaving

reference.text: Hung & Gonzalez — Progress in Aerospace Sciences, Vol.51, 2012
